# Testament of Levi — 3
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

1:1 A copy of the words of Levi, the things which he ordained to his sons, according to all they should do, and the things which would befall them until the day of judgment.
1:2 He was sound in health when he called them to him; for it had been revealed to him that he should die.
1:3 And when they were gathered together he said to them:

2:1 I Levi was conceived in Haran, and born there, and after that I came with my father to Shechem.
2:2 And I was young, about twenty years of age, when with Simeon I wrought vengeance on Hamor for the sake of our sister Dinah.
2:3 And when I was returning from the slaughter, I was greatly grieved and I lay down and slept; and I beheld a vision as Abraham our father had seen it.
2:4 And I saw the heavens opened, and an angel of the Lord spoke to me: Levi, enter!
2:5 And I entered from the first heaven into the second, and I saw water hanging between the one and the other.
2:6 And I saw a third heaven far brighter and more glorious than those two, for the height of it was incomparable.
2:7 And I said to the angel: Why is this? And the angel said to me: Marvel not, for thou shalt see another heaven far brighter still, because thou standest near unto the Lord.
2:8 Thou shalt be his minister, and shalt declare his mysteries to men, and shalt proclaim him that shall redeem Israel; and by thee and Judah shall the Lord be seen among men, saving every race.

3:1 And the angel opened to me the gates of heaven, and I saw the holy temple, and upon a throne of glory the Most High.
3:2 And he said to me: Levi, I have given thee the blessings of the priesthood until I come and sojourn in the midst of Israel.
3:3 Then the angel brought me down to the earth, and gave me a shield and a sword, and said: Execute vengeance on Shechem because of Dinah thy sister, and I will be with thee, for the Lord hath sent me.
3:4 And I slew Shechem himself first, and Simeon slew Hamor; and after that our brothers came and smote the city with the edge of the sword.
3:5 And our father heard these things and was wroth, and was grieved because the Canaanites and the Perizzites heard of it.
3:6 And we departed thence and came to Bethel.

4:1 And there I saw a second vision, as the former, after we had spent seventy days there.
4:2 And I saw seven men in white raiment saying to me: Arise, put on the robe of the priesthood, and the crown of righteousness, and the breastplate of understanding, and the garment of truth, and the plate of faith, and the turban of a sign, and the ephod of prophecy.
4:3 And they each carried one of these things and put them on me, and said: From henceforth become a priest of the Lord, thou and thy seed for ever.
4:4 And the first anointed me with holy oil, and gave me the staff of judgment.
4:5 The second washed me with pure water, and fed me with bread and wine, even the most holy things, and clad me with a holy and glorious robe.
4:6 The third clothed me with a linen vestment like an ephod.
4:7 The fourth put round me a girdle like purple.
4:8 The fifth gave me a branch of rich olive.
4:9 The sixth placed a crown on my head.
4:10 The seventh placed on my head a diadem of priesthood, and filled my hands with incense, that I might serve as priest to the Lord God.
4:11 And they said to me: Levi, thy seed shall be divided into three offices, for a sign of the glory of the Lord who is to come.
4:12 And the first portion shall be great; yea, greater than it shall none be. The second shall be in the priesthood. And the third shall be called by a new name, because a king shall arise in Judah and shall establish a new priesthood, after the fashion of the nations, to all the nations.
4:13 And his presence is beloved, as a prophet of the Most High, of the seed of Abraham our father.

5:1 Therefore everything desirable in Israel shall be for thee and for thy seed, and ye shall eat everything fair to look upon, and the table of the Lord shall thy seed apportion.
5:2 And some of them shall be high priests, and judges, and scribes; for by their mouth shall the holy place be guarded.
5:3 And when I awoke, I understood that this was like the former dream.
5:4 And I hid this also in my heart, and told it to no man upon the earth.

6:1 And after two days Judah and I went up with our father Jacob to Isaac our grandfather.
6:2 And my father's father blessed me according to all the words of the visions which I had seen.
6:3 And he would not come with us to Bethel.
6:4 And when we came to Bethel, Jacob our father had a vision concerning me, that I should be to them for a priest unto God.
6:5 And he rose up early in the morning and paid tithes of all to the Lord through me; and we came to Hebron to dwell there.
6:6 And Isaac continually called me to put me in remembrance of the law of the Lord, even as the angel of the Lord had shown me.
6:7 And he taught me the law of the priesthood: sacrifices, whole burnt offerings, first-fruits, freewill offerings, peace offerings; and each day he instructed me and was busied for my sake before the Lord.

7:1 And there shall come upon you a man who renews the law in the power of the Most High; whom you will call a deceiver, but in truth he will not be a deceiver, but a new priest whom God will appoint.
7:2 He shall execute righteous judgment upon earth for many days.
7:3 And his star shall rise in heaven as of a king, lighting up the light of knowledge as the sun the day, and he shall be magnified in the world.
7:4 He shall shine forth as the sun on the earth and shall remove all darkness from under heaven, and there shall be peace in all the earth.
7:5 The heavens shall exult in his days, and the earth shall be glad, and the clouds shall rejoice; and the knowledge of the Lord shall be poured forth upon the earth as the water of the seas; and the angels of the glory of the presence of the Lord shall be glad in him.

---
*End of Testament of Levi*
